record.name: Laniakea Supercluster
record.notes: Laniakea is a basin of attraction rather than a concentration of galaxies: the volume whose peculiar-velocity flow lines, reconstructed with a Wiener filter from Cosmicflows-2 distances, run inward to one local attractor near the Norma and Centaurus clusters. It holds the historical Local and Southern superclusters, the Pavo-Indus filament, an extension to the Ophiuchus Cluster, the Local Void and the Sculptor and other bounding voids. The point is the centroid of the attractor region, read in supergalactic Cartesian coordinates as the paper's maps are drawn; the sentence itself names no frame. The published km/s values are kept; the paper's Mpc figures convert them with its Hubble constant. The mass enclosed, in solar masses, has no unit in univ-model and is left out; the Hubble constant's uncertainty is kept in its cited sentence. The paper expects Laniakea to prove to be in motion as part of something larger.
